title: A clearer first experience
intent: Help new customers understand what the product can do, reach a useful result quickly, and return later without losing their place.
audiences: People using the product for the first time
Experienced customers returning to unfinished work

observed_signals: The request concerns interactive first-session and returning-user application screens
modality_assessment.rationale: The primary output is an interactive product workflow; screenshots are review evidence rather than the target modality.

direction_count_basis: One material tradeoff remains between a faster first outcome and more guided orientation

material_ambiguities: Whether the first session prioritizes immediate outcome or guided orientation

insight_decisions.insight: Returning users can already resume unfinished work and should not lose that favorable behavior.
insight_decisions.design_response: Create a direct returning-user route that exposes the saved object, last meaningful state, and one primary continuation action before onboarding guidance.
insight_decisions.observable_evidence: The returning-user artifact shows saved-work identity, freshness, and a direct resume action without replaying first-session steps.

working_assumptions: The first useful result is more important than exposing the complete product during the initial session

source_uncertainties.question: Which existing shortcut do experienced users rely on most?

current_strengths: Returning users can resume unfinished work
Experienced users have a fast keyboard path
current_gaps: New users cannot identify the first useful outcome
Visual hierarchy changes between onboarding steps

content_provenance.statement: Returning users can resume unfinished work

content_provenance.required_qualification: Illustrative progress value; replace with product data

shared_core: Understand current work and resume safely

routes.audience: People using the product for the first time
needs: Orientation and a useful first result

routes.audience: Experienced customers returning to unfinished work

design_debt: Spacing and state treatments are implemented locally instead of through shared tokens
preserve: Current fast path for experienced users
non_goals: Do not redesign unrelated account administration
validation_criteria: A first-time user can identify the primary action
The existing keyboard path remains available without additional steps
open_questions: Which existing shortcut do experienced users rely on most?
